falsifier: Re-scope the pragma tightly around any subset of the TU and measure the whole roster with `defake_gate.py baseline` then `fndiff --count`. This law is DISPROVED if any function's real improves and none regresses. The exact disproving evidence would be a per-function delta map showing a net real decrease; the measured map for game/sys/memcard on 2026-09-01 is the opposite (net real +622, five regressions, zero improvements) and lives in attempt.MC_memcard-opt-propagation-rescope-refuted.20260901.v1. subject: tu:game/sys/memcard
value:
A `#pragma opt_* off` with NO matching `reset` is not automatically a scoping BUG. Read it as a deliberate whole-TU compiler setting until a full-roster A/B says otherwise, and NEVER narrow one on the reasoning that 'an unscoped pragma must be a leak'.

MEASURED, game/sys/memcard. `#pragma opt_propagation off` sits at line 267 with no `reset` anywhere in the 2000-line file, so it governs all 30 functions from add_vmu_file to drawMemCardMessage. It looks exactly like scaffold somebody forgot to close, it is in no record's premise, and a work order accordingly targeted it as the TU's highest-leverage stale item. Re-scoping it (pin-compatibly: kept OFF across the three webfrank-pinned functions, ON for the other 27) produced FIVE regressions and ZERO improvements - net real 1226 -> 1848, +622 - and, decisively, it demoted TWO CURRENTLY BYTE-EXACT functions: saveMount real 0 -> 24 (EXACT -> OPERAND_DIFF) and vmu_exists real 0 -> 18 (EXACT -> STRUCTURAL). loadGauntletSave alone went 628 -> 1164.

WHY THE INFERENCE IS TEMPTING AND WRONG. The corpus already carries claim.law.LG_scaffold-pragmas-and-qualifiers-go-stale-reaudit-them-after-any-real-fix, and its thesis is true and valuable. But that law is about scaffold whose PREMISE has been invalidated by a later fix, and it explicitly warns that re-audit means MEASURE, not delete on sight. An unscoped pragma triggers a second, different intuition - a tidiness/correctness one - and that intuition has no evidence behind it. The two must not be conflated: 'this pragma is untidy' and 'this pragma is stale' are unrelated claims, and only the second is testable by the scaffold law's method. Here the untidy pragma was the correct configuration and the file's ONE genuinely dead pragma was the tidy-looking one (see below).

THE INVERSE, measured in the same pass and worth as much. The same file's `#pragma opt_lifetimes reset` at line 1420 LOOKS well-formed and load-bearing - it is a proper reset sitting exactly between two functions - and it is completely dead: its matching `off` was deleted by an earlier pass, so it restores an already-current default. Deleting it left the built object BYTE-IDENTICAL (sha256 9DAE52D5160A9595D2E45CB19737C3A7A79554EAC4D4C29D742B5EEDC0719D54 both ways). So in one file, the pragma that looked broken was load-bearing and the pragma that looked correct was inert. SYNTACTIC APPEARANCE CARRIES NO INFORMATION ABOUT A PRAGMA'S EFFECT; only a build does.

OPERATIONAL RULE. Cost to settle either question is one build. Before re-scoping any pragma, take a `defake_gate.py baseline` of the WHOLE TU, make the scope edit, and read `fndiff --count` for every function - not just the function you care about, because the functions a pragma protects are usually the ones already at real 0 and therefore invisible in any queue ranked by remaining work. A roster ranked by 'what still needs fixing' structurally cannot show you what a setting is currently BUYING.

PIN INTERACTION, and the procedure that made the experiment possible at all. A webfrank pin hash-asserts its function's pre-postprocess body, so a pragma re-scope that changes a pinned function's codegen ABORTS the build with an input-hash mismatch rather than producing a score. That abort is itself a valid measurement - it proves the setting is load-bearing for that function - but it destroys the roster measurement, because no object is produced. The working procedure is a PIN-COMPATIBLE re-scope: keep the pragma in force across every pinned function by bracketing each one individually, and vary only the unpinned remainder. That yields a full, honest per-function map with every pin intact and the build green.
